rubrics.justification: It appropriately notes that no image was provided and bases morphology on the stated Gardner score, but it inaccurately describes stage 3 as an expanded blastocyst with thinning zona (more consistent with stage 4) and overstates TE quality relative to the provided description.
It thoroughly integrates age, tubal factor diagnosis, prior live birth, endometrial thickness, BMI, ovarian response, and sperm parameters with embryo quality and prognosis.

The reasoning is structured and mostly consistent, with a plausible prognosis estimate tied to embryo and patient factors, though the morphology-stage interpretation and some strength of claims are slightly overstated.

Recommendations such as single embryo transfer and not routinely recommending PGT-A in a 28-year-old are broadly guideline-consistent, though ERA/chronic endometritis workup after a single failed transfer is somewhat premature and the blastocyst stage description is not strictly Gardner-consistent.

It gives clear practical recommendations for SET, luteal support, alcohol cessation, and future planning, but some suggestions remain somewhat generic and not all are tightly tailored to this exact scenario.
